ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the image, from left to right there are four square figures. The first square is not divided, and is 1 part; the second square is divided by one vertical line and one horizontal line into 2×2's 4 parts; the third figure is on the basis of the second, continuing to divide one part in the upper right into 4 small parts, so the total number becomes 7; the fourth figure again divides one small part further in the upper right into 4 even smaller parts, so the total number becomes 10. Reasoning: Each step is dividing the original 1 part into 4 parts. In this way the total number of parts will increase by 4−1=3. It is known that the numbers of parts of the first four figures are 1, 4, 7, 10, indeed increasing by 3 each time. Therefore the number of parts of the fifth figure is 10+3=13.

raw_record.question_text: We make a sequence of figures by dividing a square. The first four figures have 1, 4, 7 and 10 parts, respectively. How many parts will the fifth figure have?

method.method_draft: First describe the image: it shows four successive square figures. The first is an undivided square, the second is divided into a 2-by-2 grid with 4 parts, the third keeps most of that grid but subdivides the upper-right region further so the total becomes 7, and the fourth subdivides a smaller upper-right region again so the total becomes 10. Read from the text that these are the first four figures and their part counts are 1, 4, 7, and 10, and that the task asks for the fifth figure. Use the visual pattern that each step takes one existing part and divides it into 4 smaller parts, which increases the total number of parts by 3. Therefore the fifth figure has 10 + 3 = 13 parts.

推理：每一步都是把原来的1个部分分成4个部分。这样总部分数会增加4−1=3。已知前四个图形的部分数是1、4、7、10，确实每次增加3。因此第五个图形的部分数是10+3=13。
